fixture_set: 1 new selection fixture under evals/evaluating-skill-quality/tasks/: dispatch-self-guard-boundary-selection.yaml, gating dimension 5's (Progressive disclosure) new content-independent-dispatch-self-guard boundary. Formally gated (before/after, strict improve-or-reject, ordinary class -- a new rule addition, not pruning).
dispatch_mechanism: Isolated `claude -p` subprocess (CLI 2.1.246 (Claude Code)), prompt passed as a single self-contained CLI argument, run from a scratch working directory outside any repository's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md ancestry, with an isolated $HOME (per adversarial-self-audit.md's Isolation verification recipe -- new Same-run entry recorded for this exact platform/version). Two additional contamination sources were found and fixed live during this run, neither previously named in adversarial-self-audit.md's registry: (1) a `claude -p` subprocess sharing the caller's real $HOME leaks not only TaskCreate/TaskUpdate task-list state (the already-documented leak) but, in this multi-agent-messaging-capable harness, also inherits enough ambient session state (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_CODE_WEBSOCKET_AUTH_FILE_DESCRIPTOR, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION) that the dispatched process sometimes returned a bare 'waiting for the background dispatch to complete' non-answer instead of performing the review -- fixed by additionally unsetting those variables, on top of the isolated-$HOME copy. (2) Independently, a prompt instructing the dispatch to follow SKILL.md's own Subagent-dispatch Procedure caused the dispatch to attempt satisfying that instruction literally (shelling out to a nested claude -p via Bash, matching the already-known 'too slow, background polling' pattern the issue #619 split.md entry recorded) even with the tool allowed -- fixed by an explicit prompt instruction to perform the entire review synchronously in one response with no nested dispatch, and by dropping Bash from --allowedTools entirely (Read/Glob/Grep only) so no nested invocation is possible. Both fixes are disclosed here as a candidate addition to adversarial-self-audit.md's own registry, not yet made (out of scope for this gate run; a separate rubric-maintenance edit).
scorer: skills/scorer-gated-skill-edits/scripts/gitapex_score_contract.py, scoring the fixture's own output_contains/output_not_contains assertions deterministically. `gitapex_score_contract.py --compare-to 0.666667`, score 1.000000 -> `1.000000 KEEP`.

known_gaps: Only this one new selection fixture was live-dispatched; the pre-existing selection fixtures were not re-scored on both sides. This edit's diff (a pure rubric.md bullet addition to dimension 5, no reword of existing text) was reasoned content-disjoint from the pre-existing corpus by direct inspection rather than confirmed by live re-dispatch -- the same disclosed methodology this skill's own split.md log has used for a pure-insertion edit in multiple prior iterations (issues #537, #1124, #1142).
trials_per_fixture=1 -- no repeat-run variance data; a single sample generalizing correctly is not proof a weaker tier or a different sample would.

No transfer check (an adjacent model/harness re-run) was performed before this record was written -- deferred as a same-class disclosed gap to prior iterations in this same directory that also did not complete one inline.

This run also surfaced (and worked around) two contamination sources not yet reflected as their own Known entries in adversarial-self-audit.md's Isolation verification registry -- see dispatch_mechanism above for the full description. Recording that gap here rather than silently folding the workaround into 'business as usual', per this skill's own Contaminated-dispatch disclosure norm; adding the formal registry entries is separate follow-up work, not done as part of this gate run.
